Welcome
Welcome to Greatham; our stunning primary school nestled in the heart of the South Downs. We are a one-form-entry primary school catering for children from 4-11 years of age who live in Greatham and the surrounding areas (Liss, Bordon, Whitehill, Lindford, Empshott, Liphook and even Petersfield). The school was built in 1911 and celebrated its centenary in 2011!
Our school grounds are beautiful and include climbing apparatus, a forest school garden (complete with fire pit) and an extensive field. Children thoroughly enjoy using these facilities and, in particular, forest school lessons. We share a keen interest in sport, encompassing healthy, active lifestyles and we have been very successful in inter-school competitions as well as being awarded the prestigious 'Gold Sports Mark School'.
Our school values of Care, Aspire and Achieve underpin everything that we do. We have high aspirations of the children and nurture and support them to achieve academically, socially and emotionally so that they can become confident, caring individuals. Through a broad and high-quality curriculum, we aim to inspire a love of learning and a lifelong curiosity and desire to solve problems and answer questions.
Our school community encompasses the children, parents, governors, staff and we proudly work in partnership. We are passionate about building strong relationships in order to enable learning without limits. We firmly believe that each child is unique and we ensure that we get to know them well.
We trust that both you and your child will be very happy and we look forward to working with you.
If you would like to know more about us, please get in touch by email adminoffice@greatham.hants.sch.uk or by telephone 01420 538224. We will be happy to help you.
We hope that you find this website useful and informative. Paper copies of any information on this website are available free of charge on request.

pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Values
The children, parents, teachers, and governors of Greatham Primary School have a vision for the school which is…
To be a beacon of educational excellence that nurtures and supports our children academically, socially, physically and emotionally. Our goal is for every child to become a confident, caring and healthy individual who aspires to excellence in everything they do and who recognises and embraces diversity in all its forms.
To deliver a broad, high quality and inspiring curriculum that unlocks the unique potential of every child within a safe, caring and vibrant learning community.
To inspire children and leaders in a school where every child is known and able to learn without limits so they can achieve success.
Care, Aspire, Achieve…our values underpin everything we do as we meet our objectives, deliver our mission and strive to achieve our vision.
Every moment counts.
Within our safe community we foster and celebrate British Values through the key learning and social behaviours; CARE, ASPIRE and ACHIEVE. Please view the posters below to understand our focus within each behaviour.

Learning at Greatham Greatham has seven classes:

Curriculum Intention
To deliver a broad, high quality and inspiring curriculum that unlocks the unique potential of every child within a safe, caring and vibrant learning community.
To inspire children and leaders in a school where every child is known and able to learn without limits so they can achieve success.
At Greatham we aim for all children to receive a full education (UN Article 29) which is both exciting and engaging;
We organise our curriculum into half termly topics. Each topic has a lead subject area which acts as the key driver. The key drivers are historical, scientific or geographical because we recognise that our children demonstrate high levels of engagement in these areas of the curriculum. Other subjects are creatively placed to link learning rather than being equally spread across terms. We do not teach every subject in a half termly period and subjects are blocked together within a topic where appropriate (for example, 5 RE lessons may be taught over a 3 day period rather than weekly).
Whilst we are determined that the children know the associated facts for each curriculum area, our emphasis is on building the skills required to apply knowledge. This is to create both aspirational and resilient learners.

Curriculum
Curriculum Intention
We organise our curriculum into half-termly topics. Each topic has a lead subject area which acts as the key driver. The key drivers are historical, scientific or geographical, because we recognise that our children demonstrate high levels of engagement in these areas of the curriculum. Other subjects are creatively placed to link learning rather than being equally spread across terms. We do not teach every subject in a half-term period and subjects are blocked together within a topic where appropriate (for example, 5 RE lessons may be taught over a 3-day period rather than weekly).
We recognise that knowledge is the foundation of skill and application and are determined that the children know the associated facts for each curriculum area whilst building the skills required to apply knowledge. This is to create both aspirational and resilient learners.
English is mostly linked to topic themes and key texts are carefully selected in order to drive the learning. We recognise that outcomes for our children are stronger when the link between English text and topic is clear. Maths, PE and Spanish are taught separately. We endeavour to fill each topic with rich first-hand purposeful experiences, and we make meaningful links between subjects. An emphasis on understanding vocabulary is key in all subjects. Environments and expertise beyond the classroom are actively encouraged and within topics we are both flexible and responsive to individual needs and interests. Below you can download our curriculum map.
Alongside all curriculum areas, we teach children about safeguarding themselves and others. This is also taught explicitly. You can see our explicit teaching of safeguarding by clicking on the link below:
Explicit teaching of safeguarding
All children undertake a series of Forest School lessons every year. Our Forest School leader is a member of staff and has been fully trained to deliver the programme. You can find out about our Forest School curriculum by clicking the link below:
Forest school learning journey
For reference, here is a link to the National Curriculum
We are proud to have strong SMSC education in school. Our caring school ethos is built upon integrated opportunities for SMSC throughout the school day as well as within curriculum subjects. British Values are promoted as part of this. Some of the ways in which we achieve high quality SMSC are:
Every class undertakes a unit of RE work each half term following the Hampshire Living Difference IV curriculum. We organise the Living Difference framework as follows:
Link to Greatham School RE Overview
Link to Hampshire Living Difference IV.
Parents have the right to withdraw their children from both collective worship and also RE lessons although our school does not recommend this. Requests for withdrawal must be made in writing and addressed to the Headteacher.
We teach non-core subjects by ensuring we teach key information (knowledge) then plan for pupils to use subject specific skills to apply this learnt knowledge. We plan these subject specific skills at an age appropriate level so that pupils can develop them as they progress through our school. The poster below demonstrates how we get our pupils to think deeper and make our curriculum richer and more engaging for the pupils.
Here are the skills matrices for our non-core subjects.
School Trips We aim for each year group to have visits that are carefully interwoven with their topic. We choose experiences that are not only linked to our topics and are enjoyable for the children, but most importantly, will enhance and extend learning. Trips and may change and develop as we explore our children's interests and each topic.

SEND
Special Educational Needs & Disability (SEND) Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCo) organises help for any child who may need additional support. The Special Needs Assistant works with children who need support beyond the classroom to enable continued development in all areas of their learning. The staff will take individuals or groups of children, following work planned on a PLP (Personal Learning Plan). This could be on phonic, spelling or numeracy support. The schools ELSA (Educational Literacy Support Assistant) is able to work on listening and social skills. Other professionals who are based outside the school, work closely with the learning support team - such as educational psychologist (EP), speech and language therapist (SaLT), school nurses and parent support advisor (PSA), who can offer further specialist help if and where needed. Diversity and Inclusion
Diversity and Inclusion
As part of our ongoing commitment to developing and sustaining an inclusive culture and ethos in school, we are an active part of the county's work group. This includes nominating three children each year from year 5 who work with me to act as advocates for rights and equality.
Throughout the year, their role is to reflect on and improve the way in which the school:
Here is a sample of the work they have done.
We have signed a commitment document that was written by the county diversity team that encapsulates all of the work that we undertake in this area. I feel it is important to share this commitment with you and I have therefore copied and pasted it below. If there is anything you would like us to develop/ focus on/ deliver within this area, we would love to hear from you. As always, please email me directly on j.goman@greatham.hants.sch.uk;
We undertake this commitment in the understanding that this is one part of a long and sustained journey for our communities, intended to supplement work that we already do, and provide a forum for us to work collaboratively on a shared vision.
Settings within the partnership are committed to achieving this overarching aim by:
As part of our commitment, we undertake to use the self-evaluation tool to evaluate our existing practice; identify areas of good practice which can be shared with others; identify areas for development and seek appropriate support; and attend relevant IDP events, e.g. conference, training.

Welcome to our FROGS section! (FRiends of Greatham School) Hello and welcome to FROGS - Friends of Greatham School that is! As a parent with a child(ren) at the school you will naturally have the best interests of the school at heart-and so do we...that is why every parent is included in FROGS once their child joins the school. If you wish to support further then why not come along to our fundraising committee meetings. They are informal yet structured; fun and relaxed; usually include food and drink AND you will not be expected or pressured to do something unless you want to, but; your input and perspective are invaluable.
